slug_convention: The :latest tag is the default for any model and MUST be omitted from model names and slugs. Only explicit non-default tags (e.g. :14b, :q8_0, :bf16) are included.

methodology_notes.layer2_raw_vs_chat: Layer 2 (HumanEval-CS, 158 tasks) historically uses scripts/benchmark_coding_layer2.py which calls /api/generate with raw:true. This bypasses the model's chat template / RENDERER / PARSER and sends the C# function signature as a raw completion prefix. Completion-friendly models (granite4, OmniCoder, qwen-coder, gemma3, shenwen-coderV2) handle this well and score 25-50%. Chat-tuned and thinking-default models (gemma4 family, gpt-oss, glm-4.7-flash-reap, lfm2.5-thinking, LFM2, phi4-mini) score 1-10% because they cannot interpret the raw prefix without their chat wrappers. For these models, also run scripts/benchmark_coding_layer2_chat.py which uses /api/chat (template applied, num_predict=4096, num_ctx=8192, reasoning_effort=low for gpt-oss). Chat-mode results are stored in coding-{slug}-chat.json and listed alongside the raw-mode score in this file. Headline 'L2' for chat-tuned models should use the chat-mode score; raw-mode is a methodological footnote.
methodology_notes.layer3_think_variants: Layer 3 (.NET, 50 tasks) coding runner defaults to think:false via task_runner.py. To run a paired think:true variant, set CODING_BENCH_THINK=true; the runner suffixes the checkpoint with '-think' so both variants are preserved (coding-{slug}.json and coding-{slug}-think.json). Some models (granite4 family, qwen3-coder-next) reject think:true with 'does not support thinking' and produce a 0/50 file that should be deleted. Other models (gpt-oss, lfm2.5-thinking, glm-4.7-flash-reap-toolfix) ignore think:false and still emit reasoning; their no-think baselines are effectively think runs and the -think variant is redundant. See memory/project_ollama_think_quirks.md for the full matrix.

backend_notes.codegemma:latest: Google CodeGemma 9B (Q4_0, 8.5GB), instruction-tuned code model. Strix: 35.21 tok/s, 8.5GB VRAM, 0.18s load. Quality quick suite 4/11 (coding 4/5, tool 0/4, agentic 0/2 â€” no native tool-calling support at all, both plan-agent and direct tool-call tasks fail outright). Coding L2 (HumanEval-CS, 158 tasks): RAW 50/158 (0.316), CHAT 51/158 (0.323) â€” raw and chat modes agree closely, unlike gemma3/gemma4-family models with template-bypass artifacts; either mode is trustworthy here. Coding L3 (.NET, 50 tasks, think:false): 21/50 (0.382) weighted. Ranks solidly mid-pack for single-shot code gen (below top-5 L2 ~0.49-0.52 and top-5 L3 ~0.80-0.86) but well above the field floor, and notably ahead of several much larger/newer models on L2 (e.g. beats qwen3.5:4b 0.291, shenwen-coderV2 0.266, devstral-small-2 0.234). Zero tool/agentic capability is the standout weakness vs top-5 models (qwen3.6, qwen3.6:27b, devstral-small-2 all score 11/11 quality). FINE-TUNE VIABILITY: reasonable small-model (9B, 8.5GB) target specifically for C#/.NET code completion or bolting on tool-calling via SFT â€” its underlying single-shot coding competence (comparable to mid-tier 14-27B models) is real and non-trivial, and the tool-calling gap is a well-understood, fixable fine-tuning target rather than a fundamental capability ceiling. GOTCHA (2026-07-12): a stale `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434` (no scheme, invalid client target) in the shell silently produced a 0/11 quality score via the harness's broad except-and-continue error handling before this was caught and fixed â€” always confirm OLLAMA_HOST is a valid `http://host:port` before trusting a near-zero score.
backend_notes.codegemma:2b: Google CodeGemma 2B (Q4_0, 1.8GB), BASE/completion-only model â€” NOT instruction-tuned, unlike codegemma:latest. Strix: reported 117.82 tok/s is an ARTIFACT (eval_count=4, the model degenerated into short garbage almost immediately on the throughput probe's natural-language prompt; not a real steady-state rate). Quality quick suite: genuine 0/11 (confirmed via manual probe: both raw-generate and /api/chat on natural-language/instruction prompts degenerate into repetition or garbage like a bare 'ipynb\n' â€” this is real base-model behaviour, not a harness/env bug, unlike the codegemma:latest 0/11 false-negative below). Also tried the model's proper FIM special tokens (`<|fim_prefix|>`/`<|fim_suffix|>`/`<|fim_middle|>`) manually via raw generate to see if genuine FIM formatting would help â€” they are NOT registered as special tokens by this Ollama GGUF pull (echoed back as literal text), so FIM-templated prompting is not usable through this harness/model pull either. Coding L2 RAW (HumanEval-CS structured prefix, i.e. its home-turf task shape): 26/158 (0.165) â€” genuinely useful, non-zero: the dataset's natural `class Problem { method(...) {` prefix shape is closer to what a FIM-only base model expects than an ad-hoc bare prompt. Coding L2 CHAT: 3/158 (0.019) â€” expected collapse, confirms it cannot use instruction/chat framing at all. Coding L3 (.NET, agentic/multi-file): 0/50 (0.000) â€” genuine hard zero, consistent with total lack of instruction-following (L3 requires following natural-language task descriptions, not just completing a fill-in-the-blank prefix). FINE-TUNE VIABILITY: NOT a good target for general instruction-following/agentic coding â€” you'd be doing full instruction-tuning from scratch, not adapting existing capability. Could be viable narrowly for raw FIM-style IDE autocomplete (small footprint, 1.8GB, fast load) given its non-trivial 16.5% raw-completion score, but that is a materially different use case than a coding assistant and untested here beyond the L2 raw dataset shape.

CODING (figures 2026-06-24, qwen3.5:9b Q4_K_M 6.6GB, gen on T5500 RTX 3060 via OLLAMA_HOST, build/test on Framework â€” same cross-machine setup as Qwythos so directly comparable): L2 CHAT 67/158 (0.424) â€” trusted L2 number; L2 RAW 42/158 (0.266) â€” ARTIFACT (raw completion mode on this instruct-tuned model emits Java-ish code when unanchored, e.g. `public static void main`/`Scanner`; use L2-CHAT instead). Fresh same-day re-run after hardening the raw harness; the prior 61/158 was a 2026-04-17 figure from an EARLIER model pull (current build re-pulled 2026-06-23, digest 6488c96fa5fa), so the two are NOT comparable. L3 (.NET) â€” CORRECTED 2026-06-24 (the earlier 3/50 was an ARTIFACT of the test_project NuGet-restore contamination: 0/44 test_project tasks built; fixed via the per-template nuget.config bypass): no-think 11/50 (0.218 weighted, 14/50 build), think 5/50 (0.109, 6/50 build) â€” THINK HURT L3 (11->5), USE THE NO-THINK BASELINE. Builds now 14/50 (were 0 under contamination); remaining fails are genuine model build/test misses. Think behaviour: CLEAN â€” thinks by default, thinking emitted to a SEPARATE 'thinking' API field (NOT <think> in content), think:false suppresses it and works; content always clean so coding extractors need no special handling. KEY COMPARISON (base vs empero-ai Qwythos-9B fine-tune, BOTH same cross-machine setup â†’ apples-to-apples): base wins L2-chat (67 vs 62); the fine-tune wins L2-raw (42 vs 50) and DECISIVELY wins L3 â€” no-think 25 vs 11, think 15 vs 5 (~2.3x). This REVERSES the earlier 'base beats the finetune' read (which rested on contaminated L3 + L2-chat alone): on framework-level .NET (L3) the Qwythos fine-tune is clearly the stronger coder; base only edges ahead on single-method L2-chat. This is exactly why the differentiator for this model class is the agentic/tool/long-context Layer 4 suite (docs/agentic-tool-longcontext-benchmark-plan.md), not single-shot code gen. LAYER 4 T5 (long-ctx VRAM/throughput, T5500 RTX 3060 12GB, default f16 KV, 2026-06-24): full 128K context fits 100% on-GPU at 9.93GB (weights ~5.5GB + KV ~0.34GB/10k tokens â‰ˆ 34KiB/tok, GQA-4/head_dim-256/no-sliding-window); 256K spills (16.3GB, only 65% on GPU â†’ would need Strix 128GB or KV-quant, untested). Decode degrades gracefully 43.0(4K)/40.7(16K)/37.7(32K)/33.1(64K)/26.7(128K) tok/s; prefill 1453â†’875 tok/s. ANSWERS the headline 'long context without massive VRAM?': YES to 128K on a 12GB card. See results/longcontext-qwen3.5_9b.json + scripts/benchmark_longcontext.py. LAYER 4 T1/T2/T3 (tool-use + agentic, gen on T5500, 2026-06-24): T1 tool-correctness 6/6 (single/multi-distractor/nested/parallel/abstention/sequential-dep all pass), T2 ReAct loop 2/2 (multi-step + error-recovery both correct), T3 agentic C# 3/3 (read/edit/build/test loop, ~6-7 steps/task, green first try). STRIKING CONTRAST with its single-shot coding (L2-raw 27%, L3 22%): this model class is BUILT for agentic/tool use, which Layers 1-3 cannot see and Layer 4 does. See results/layer4-tools-qwen3.5_9b.json + layer4-agentic-qwen3.5_9b.json.

VibeThinker-3B + LoRA (r=32/a=64, 7 target modules, bf16, packing seq2048, adamw_torch, 3 epochs) on 5k completion-style C# examples from The Stack v1 dedup (scripts/lora/build_stack_csharp_dataset.py; 4500 train / 500 holdout). Deployed via GGUF (f16, convert_hf_to_gguf on T5500) -> ollama create (GGUF import; Ollama's safetensors converter fails 'untrusted mount point' on T5500 â€” see PLATFORM_QUIRKS). RESULTS (gen on T5500 GPU via OLLAMA_HOST, build/test on Framework): Coding L2 CHAT 20/158 (0.127); Coding L3 (.NET) 0/50. VERDICT: did NOT clear the >=40/158 phase-1 gate, and is a SLIGHT REGRESSION vs base VibeThinker (25/158) â€” narrow 5k completion-style LoRA mildly eroded base reasoning (catastrophic forgetting) while teaching the desired raw-C#-output behavior (no <think>, no prose/markdown â€” confirmed). L2 failure mix: 85 build-fail (model syntax errors + inconsistent output format, e.g. sometimes emits its own Main), 50 build-OK-wrong-answer, 2 runtime exc, 1 timeout, 20 PASS. L3 0/50 expected: phase-1 did not target ASP.NET/EF/MassTransit APIs (phase-2 goal). NOTE: required an L2-chat harness fix (commit 408b62f) to handle bare re-emitted methods (no class Problem wrapper) â€” without it the fine-tune scored an artifactual 0/158. NEXT ITER: scale phase-1 data (50k+), mitigate forgetting (lower lr/rank or mix instruction+diverse data), improve Stack example quality (many train bodies were low-quality raw functions).
